0x1400133a0 calls CreateServiceW at 0x14001347f using caller-provided service configuration and a SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS type.
0x140012e00 launches the configured child through CreateProcessW at 0x140013140 and reports service status.

Process termination, token adjustment, service creation, registry configuration and log rotation support the wrapper role and remain detected.

nssm.judgement: BENIGN service administration utility. No embedded hostile payload, covert credential collection, C2 or unauthorized service target established. Operator-selected service arguments and host deployment context are absent. An attempted independent upstream ZIP retrieval returned HTTP 503; the verdict does not claim byte identity to an independently downloaded NSSM build.

dd80.identity: Trojanized Tencent GameLoop UnInstall.exe facade; final malware family not established
trace: PE entry VA 0x684ec0 starts with CALL 0x967000 into a writable/executable .reloc section.

0x967000 saves registers and recovers its location with CALL/POP. From 0x967019 it applies per-dword XOR/ADD/SUB/NOT transforms, advancing in 0x400-byte blocks until 0x8c000 bytes are decoded at 0x8da600.
At 0x9678c1, CALL 0x924554 hands execution to the decoded region. Unicorn was stopped before this call; the decoded stage was inspected statically.
The decoded stage uses paired JE/JNE branches to conceal control flow. At 0x920f7e it reads the PEB; module/export resolution hashes names with rotate-by-19 plus addition (e.g. 0x9211e7).
The buffer at 0x8da884 is LZNT1-compressed. Independent decompression produces 404992 bytes beginning with a fake PNG signature, with a relocated PE-header pointer at offset 8.
The stage accepts both MZ/PE and fake PNG headers: 0x923b98 checks PNG, 0x924169 checks its second dword, and 0x924180 reads the alternate header pointer.

0x9238e4 validates/parses the image, allocates memory, copies sections, relocates addresses, resolves imports, and configures page permissions. The export-lookup path at 0x92467f..0x9246f6 resolves and calls an export. The reconstructed DLL exports _a@4.
dd80.judgement: MALICIOUS: entry-point graft, encrypted native code, disguised executable headers and a manual PE activation path are unrelated to uninstalling GameLoop. No live execution, successful outbound connection or final payload family is asserted.

Recovered bytes were placed at the requested extracted-member path.
trace: initServerProcess returns an IPC message handler. A startServer message creates the HTTP(S) server, optional WebSocket server and configured listener.
The request handler serves project files, compiler responses and development client assets. WebSocket messages carry rebuild/HMR data.

Bundled browser-opening code uses child_process/execa to discover or launch the default browser. Editor requests validate editor names and file existence; the published editor API in this bundle is mocked.
SHA-1, random bytes and compression support the bundled WebSocket implementation. Generic HTTP, process creation and encoding capabilities are accurate and retained.
stencil.judgement: BENIGN development tooling. No concealed payload, arbitrary remote shell tasking or credential collection was established. Listener address and project configuration come from the caller; actual deployment context was not supplied.

sanitizers.identity: Four CJS/ESM/browser bundles of sanitize-html, HTML parsers, URL/CSS validation and entity decoding
sanitizers.trace: Exports sanitizeHtml(html), returns empty for falsy input, then invokes sanitize-html with a restricted tag/attribute/scheme allowlist and nonTextTags excluding script/style/textarea/option/xmp. Encoded tables and generated parser code are data and bundler output. No credential-to-send or payload-to-execution chain was found.
sanitizers.judgement: BENIGN individual library members; enclosing archive conviction is retained.

coverage_and_disagreements: dd80 now fires two hostile traits across anti-static and evasion, plus the suspicious decoder. Deeper decoded-stage hashing, LZNT1, disguised-header parsing and manual mapping are documented, but no ciphertext-specific duplicate rules were invented for encrypted operations unavailable in static facts.

Both archives remain convicted as instructed; no new hostile traits were fabricated from their labels. The inspected NSSM, Stencil and sanitizer members do not independently justify hostile coverage. Their enclosing archive convictions therefore remain context/rule disagreements for this static analysis.

The dd80 model probability rises from 0.94267774 to 0.99250776, yet its calibrated level remains -1 (unflagged/benign), despite verified malicious behavior and two hostile traits. Reported as a classifier miss, not repaired by duplicate traits.

NSSM first cached scan included 240 findings and risk 81. Fresh baseline/current Atomscan scans each emit 195 findings (risk 79 -> 40) with exactly the two intended ID replacements. Independent Cleave scans confirm that same diff. The initial apparent loss of derivative aliases/low-tier findings is not caused by changed YAML matching; original capability atoms remain present.
No attack traits were lost on the 16 focused baseline/current controls, including existing out-of-batch miner/service fixtures, the Lua carrier consumer and shortcut proxy attack.
